{{nihongo|'''Mure Shrine'''|牟禮神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Ibaraki, Osaka|Q502403|qid=Q502403}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine rank}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. {{nihongo|'''Mure Shrine'''|牟禮神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993|lt=Takehaya Susanoo no Mikoto}} (たてはやすさのおのみこと)
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame-no-Koyane no Mikoto}} (あめのこやねのみこと)

== History ==
In the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'' lists it as “Mure Shrine, {{ill|Shimashimo district|Q10976940|qid=Q10976940}}, Settsu Province,” and it is ranked as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

In the ''{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}'', in the section on {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, there is the passage “Miko Ōnakatsuhiko no Mikoto is the ancestral deity of Mure no Wake,” leading to a theory that the shrine originally enshrined {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōnakatsuhiko no Mikoto}} (おおなかつひこのみこと), the ancestor of the Mure clan.<ref>However, the relationship between “Mure no Wake” and this locality is not clear (from the “Mure Village” entry in ''Place Names of Osaka Prefecture'').</ref> Nevertheless, it is said that in order to avoid the temple and shrine burnings carried out by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}}, the shrine falsely claimed its enshrined deities were {{ill|Gozu Tennō|Q11570247|qid=Q11570247}} and the {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805}}, whom Nobunaga revered, and this claim remained thereafter.

In {{ill|Hōei|Q1145262|qid=Q1145262}} 1 ({{ill|1704|Q6824|qid=Q6824}}), it was returned from the Mure settlement to the Nakamura settlement.

In {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern system of shrine ranks}}, it was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

In {{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}} 14 ({{ill|1939|Q18639|qid=Q18639}}), due to river improvement works on the {{ill|Ai River|Q11450512|qid=Q11450512}}, the shrine was relocated to its present site. In Shōwa 15 ({{ill|1940|Q18633|qid=Q18633}}), it received and repurposed the building of the north-facing Hachiman Shrine, a subsidiary shrine of {{ill|Ikukunitama Shrine|Q11574477|qid=Q11574477}}, which had been built in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 11 ({{ill|1606|Q6747|qid=Q6747}}) by {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|Q1882775|qid=Q1882775}}, as its shrine hall. In Shōwa 54 ({{ill|1979|Q2484|qid=Q2484}}), the main hall was restored.
